이것.t: In speech 이것 usually becomes 이거: 이거 얼마예요? (How much is this?)

같이.x: Shall we watch a movie together this weekend?

탁구.x: I played ping-pong with coworkers during lunch.
탁구.t: Pronounced [탁꾸] — ㄱ after ㄱ becomes tense.

도시락.ex: 저는 매일 회사에 도시락을 싸 가요.
도시락.x: I pack a lunch to take to work every day.
도시락.e: Convenience-store 도시락 are a popular, cheap lunch in Korea.
도시락.t: Use 싸다 'to pack, wrap' with it: 도시락을 싸다 means to pack a lunch.

방문하다.x: I'm scheduled to visit a client's company tomorrow.

자원봉사.ex: 올림픽 때 많은 대학생들이 자원봉사를 했어요.
자원봉사.x: Many college students volunteered during the Olympics.

격려.ex: 선생님의 격려 덕분에 끝까지 할 수 있었어요.
격려.x: Thanks to my teacher's encouragement, I was able to see it through.
격려.t: Pronounced [경녀]: nasalization changes both ㄱ and ㄹ.

갈수록.forms: 갈수록 + 더/점점: 날이 갈수록 · 시간이 갈수록
갈수록.m: increasingly, more and more as time goes on
갈수록.ex: 시간이 갈수록 한국어 공부가 더 재미있어져요.
갈수록.x: As time goes on, studying Korean gets more and more fun.
갈수록.e: 가다 'to go' + -ㄹ수록 'the more...': 'the further it goes'.
갈수록.t: Usually paired with -아/어지다: 갈수록 어려워져요 (it keeps getting harder).

먹거리.m: food, things to eat (at a festival or market)
먹거리.ex: 이 축제에는 맛있는 먹거리가 정말 많아요.
먹거리.x: There are lots of tasty things to eat at this festival.
먹거리.e: 먹다 'to eat' + -거리 'material, stuff for', as in 볼거리 'things to see'.
먹거리.t: Pronounced [먹꺼리]. Long considered nonstandard, it was accepted as standard in 2011 alongside 먹을거리.

리더십.x: Our new team leader has really outstanding leadership.
리더십.e: From English 'leadership'; Koreans often say 리더십이 있다 — to have leadership.

증가세.ex: 온라인 쇼핑 이용자가 계속 증가세를 보이고 있습니다.
증가세.x: Online shopping users continue to show an upward trend.
증가세.e: Literally 'increase momentum'; -세 = trend: 증가세, 감소세, 상승세.
증가세.t: Typical news phrase: 증가세를 보이다 — to show an upward trend.

법원.ex: 법원은 그 회사에 벌금을 내라고 했어요.
법원.x: The court ordered the company to pay a fine.
법원.t: Pronounced [버붠] — the ㅂ links to the next syllable.

장관.x: The Minister of Education held a press conference.
장관.e: Literally 'chief official'—like a U.S. cabinet secretary.
장관.t: A different word 장관 means 'magnificent sight', as in 장관을 이루다.

낙담.x: I failed the interview, but I didn't get too discouraged.
낙담.e: Literally 'your gallbladder drops'; the gallbladder was thought to be the seat of courage.

속이 타다.forms: 속이 타요 · 속이 탔어요 · 속을 태우다 (to make someone anxious)
속이 타다.m: to be anxious, to be worried sick, to be on pins and needles
속이 타다.ex: 아이와 연락이 안 돼서 속이 타요.
속이 타다.x: I can't reach my child, and I'm worried sick.
속이 타다.e: 타다 = to burn; literally 'one's insides burn' with worry.

경비실.m: security office, guard booth (in an apartment complex)
경비실.x: Please leave the package at the security office.
경비실.e: Literally 'guard room'. -실 = room: 경비실, 화장실, 사무실.
경비실.t: In Korean apartment complexes, the 경비실 often holds parcels for residents who are out.

(이)야말로.forms: 이야말로 after a consonant (건강이야말로) · 야말로 after a vowel (저야말로) · 저야말로 감사하죠
(이)야말로.m: truly, precisely, (it is) none other than
(이)야말로.x: Health is truly the most precious wealth.
(이)야말로.e: An extra-strong form of the emphatic particle (이)야: 'X, if anything, is the one'.
(이)야말로.t: 저야말로 'It's me who should (thank you / apologize)' is a very common polite reply: A: 감사합니다. B: 저야말로 감사하죠.

경질.x: The president replaced the minister who had caused the problem.
경질.t: A homonym 경질 means 'hardness'; in politics it always means replacing an official.

공중도덕.ex: 지하철에서 큰 소리로 통화하는 것은 공중도덕에 어긋나요.
공중도덕.x: Talking loudly on the phone on the subway goes against public etiquette.

직결되다.m: to be directly linked, to lead directly to
직결되다.x: Health is directly linked to quality of life.

한가롭다.ex: 주말 오후에 공원에서 한가롭게 책을 읽었어요.
한가롭다.x: I spent a weekend afternoon leisurely reading a book in the park.
한가롭다.t: 한가하다 means having free time; 한가롭다 describes a calm, leisurely mood or scene.

교수법.x: The teacher applied a new teaching method to the class.
교수법.t: Pronounced [교수뻡] — 법 is tensed after a compound.

석차.x: My class rank went up a lot on this exam.

고위직.ex: 올해도 고위직 공무원들의 재산이 모두 공개되었습니다.
고위직.x: This year, too, the assets of all high-ranking officials were made public.

누워서 침 뱉기.forms: 누워서 침 뱉기예요 · 누워서 침 뱉기나 마찬가지예요
누워서 침 뱉기.m: an act that backfires on oneself, shooting oneself in the foot (lit. spitting while lying on one's back)
누워서 침 뱉기.ex: 밖에서 회사 욕을 하는 건 누워서 침 뱉기예요.
누워서 침 뱉기.x: Badmouthing your own company to outsiders just backfires on you.
누워서 침 뱉기.e: If you spit upward while lying on your back, it falls right back onto your own face.
누워서 침 뱉기.t: Pronounced [누워서 침 밷끼]. Typically about criticizing your own family, team or company in public, which ends up shaming you. Don't mix it up with 누워서 떡 먹기 'a piece of cake'.
nb: 가는 말이 고와야 오는 말이 곱다

법무사.x: People usually leave real estate registration to a judicial scrivener.
법무사.t: Pronounced [범무사] by nasalization; a 법무사 prepares legal filings but is not a trial lawyer (변호사).

법인세.ex: 정부는 기업 투자를 늘리기 위해 법인세를 낮췄습니다.
법인세.x: The government lowered the corporate tax to boost business investment.
법인세.e: 법인 'legal person' means a corporation; add 세 'tax.'

영사.x: I lost my passport, so I got help from the consul.
영사.e: Literally 'one who oversees affairs' for citizens abroad.
영사.t: 영사 (consul) handles citizens and visas; 대사 (ambassador) represents the country.

학살.ex: 그 마을에서 민간인 학살이 일어났다는 보도가 나왔습니다.
학살.x: There were reports that a massacre of civilians took place in that village.

막후.ex: 그는 막후에서 협상을 성사시킨 핵심 인물입니다.
막후.x: He is the key figure who made the deal happen behind the scenes.
막후.t: Pronounced [마쿠]; usually 막후에서 or 막후 + noun, like 막후 실세.

조현병.ex: 조현병은 꾸준히 치료하면 증상을 관리할 수 있어요.
조현병.x: Schizophrenia symptoms can be managed with consistent treatment.
조현병.e: Literally 'tuning-string illness' — the mind as an instrument out of tune.
조현병.t: Since 2011 조현병 has replaced the stigmatizing older term 정신분열증.

연산장치.ex: 연산장치는 컴퓨터 안에서 계산을 담당하는 부분이에요.
연산장치.x: The arithmetic unit is the part of a computer that handles calculations.
연산장치.e: Literally 'calculation device'; 장치 means a device or apparatus.

향가.ex: 향가는 신라 시대에 향찰로 기록된 노래예요.
향가.x: Hyangga are songs from the Silla era recorded in hyangchal script.
향가.e: Literally 'hometown songs' — native Korean songs, as opposed to Chinese poetry.

성토하다.m: to denounce publicly, to condemn (in a group)
성토하다.x: Residents loudly denounced the development plan at the public hearing.
성토하다.e: Literally 'attack with voices': a group criticizing something loudly.

야릇하다.ex: 그는 나를 보며 야릇한 미소를 지었어요.
야릇하다.x: He looked at me with a strange smile.
야릇하다.t: Can hint at something sexual (야릇한 분위기), so use 이상하다 or 묘하다 for plain 'strange'.

삼인성호.m: a lie repeated enough becomes accepted as truth
삼인성호.ex: 삼인성호라고, 거짓 소문도 계속 퍼지면 사실처럼 믿게 돼요.
삼인성호.x: As they say, if three people say there's a tiger, a rumor starts to seem true.
삼인성호.e: If three people claim there's a tiger in the market, people believe it.
